services.desc: NOTE: the H.N.Greenwell Store Museum is currently hosting Martha Greenwell’s Mouse House Christmas Village Exhibit. Hours are posted to our social media pages. Constructed by Englishman Henry Nicholas Greenwell in 1870, the store once served the immigrant community with supplies and goods needed in the remote Kona Districts. From his headquarters here at the Greenwell Store, H.N. Greenwell amassed thousands of acres of ranch land where he and his sons helped to develop the Kona ranching industry of the late 19th century. services.desc: The Kona Historical Society offers a beautiful pasture setting for any special event. Our Kalukalu site is located at a cool elevation (1,500 feet) and includes an ocean view, native plant forest, majestic monkeypod and magnolia trees, an authentic Portuguese stone oven, stone ruins, and the historic H.N. Greenwell Store that dates from 1870. The pasture and old trees, the stone structures, and the view of the ocean beyond, provide many beautiful venues for ceremonies and photographs. Your guests will enjoy the tranquility of an authentic ranch setting, rural in nature, yet conveniently located. If the programs and guidelines listed below will not work for your classroom, please email Public Programs Assistant at Programs@konahistorical.org to discuss options.
